title: fix(crashlytics): stop Android FlutterJNI detach renderer crash after video surfaces
body:
## Crashlytics evidence

Crashlytics issue: `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a`

Console: https://console.firebase.google.com/project/openvine-co/crashlytics/app/android:co.openvine.app/issues/d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a?&time=1776614940000:1777219740000

Window queried with Firebase MCP: `2026-04-19T16:09:00Z` to `2026-04-26T16:09:00Z`

Impact in that window:

- Events: 31
- Impacted users: 15
- Sessions: 31
- First seen: `1.0.4`
- Last seen: `1.0.8`
- Signal: regressed; Crashlytics says it was closed on `2026-03-08` and regressed on `2026-03-19` in `1.0.7 (497)`.

Sample event:

- Event: `projects/972941478875/apps/1:972941478875:android:c716006682f92d9444b5fe/events/69EE0CF801F5000127E39EE7C625DF0C_2211500816387455056`
- Event time: `2026-04-26T13:12:38Z`
- App version: `1.0.8 (2513)`
- Device: Moto G Power 2025, Android `16`
- Process state: foreground
- Breadcrumb path: video-editor -> video-metadata -> pooled-video-feed repeated

Exception:

```text
java.lang.RuntimeException: Cannot execute operation because FlutterJNI is not attached to native.
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.ensureAttachedToNative (FlutterJNI.java:515)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame (FlutterJNI.java:1013)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer.scheduleEngineFrame (FlutterRenderer.java:1324)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage (FlutterRenderer.java:633)
at FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer$PerImageReader.lambda$new$0 (FlutterRenderer.java:517)
at android.media.ImageReader$1.run (ImageReader.java:951)
```

## Start here

This is not the already-filed back navigation issue by itself. Existing issue #2796/PR #2795 guarded app MethodChannel back navigation after engine detach. This crash is in Flutter renderer / `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer`, probably tied to Android platform views or texture-backed video surfaces still producing frames after engine detach/surface disposal.

Likely code areas:

- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerViewFactory.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/divine_video_player_widget.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player` lifecycle if pooled feed uses platform/texture rendering on Android.
- `mobile/android/app/src/main/kotlin/co/openvine/app/MainActivity.kt` only if engine/activity lifecycle ordering is involved.

Relevant local context:

- `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.dispose()` removes callbacks/listeners and releases `textureEntry`.
- Android platform views use `PlatformViewLink` / `AndroidViewSurface` in `divine_video_player_widget.dart`.
- `DivineVideoPlayerPlugin` pauses players on lifecycle pause/resume but only disposes all on engine detach.

## Investigation requirements

Follow root-cause first. Do not assume the previous FlutterJNI back-button fix covers this.

- Reproduce or instrument Android lifecycle while video editor/metadata and pooled feed surfaces are active.
- Trace whether `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer` corresponds to `Texture` usage, Android hybrid composition, or Flutter engine internals triggered by our video widgets.
- Verify disposal order: Flutter widget removed -> platform view disposed -> ExoPlayer surface cleared -> texture released -> engine detached.
- Confirm whether any `Surface`, `SurfaceTextureEntry`, `PlayerView`, or ExoPlayer instance can emit frame callbacks after the Flutter engine is detached.
- Compare event variants in Crashlytics if needed; there are multiple variants under this same issue.

## Suggested fix direction

Possible areas to validate:

- Ensure every Android video surface clears the player and releases the surface before engine/activity detach.
- Add lifecycle-aware stop/dispose guards for video players on `onDetachedFromActivity`, not only `onDetachedFromEngine`.
- Avoid retaining `PlayerView` / `Surface` references beyond view disposal.
- If using texture output, explicitly detach the video surface and stop rendering before `textureEntry.release()`.

## Verification

- Add Android unit tests where practical around plugin/view dispose ordering.
- Run `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` tests and relevant Android tests.
- Manually test rapid navigation: video editor -> metadata -> pooled feed -> background/foreground -> close app.
- After release, confirm Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` stops receiving events.

- Breadcrumb path: app startup -> welcome -> feed first batch received

Crash thread:

```text
Thread: mpv/mpv core (crashed)
at __pthread_kill
at pthread_kill

at dart::SimpleHashMap::Lookup(void*, unsigned int, bool) (hashmap.cc:22)
at DLRT_GetFfiCallbackMetadata (assert.h:31)
at append_event
at setproperty_fn
at mp_dispatch_queue_process
at mp_wait_events
at run_playloop
at mp_play_files
at core_thread
```

## Start here

Likely code areas:

- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/controllers/player_pool.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/controllers/video_feed_controller.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/widgets/pooled_video_feed.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/widgets/pooled_video_player.dart`
- Any app lifecycle/background handling for pooled video playback.

There is already code acknowledging related media_kit/mpv FFI lifecycle risk:

- `PlayerPool.stopAll()` mentions native mpv callbacks firing on invalidated Dart FFI handles during hot reload.
- `VideoFeedController.dispose()` tries to remove `Video` widgets before disposing native players.
- The crash is in background process state, so this may not be limited to hot reload.

## Investigation requirements

Follow root-cause first. This issue should not be treated as a generic media_kit crash without proving the lifecycle path.

- Trace all dispose/background paths for pooled players and `VideoController` / `Player` ownership.
- Verify whether native mpv callbacks can still target Dart after controllers/notifiers are disposed or after the app backgrounds.
- Check whether backgrounding should pause/stop pooled playback earlier than current logic.
- Check whether feed/player widgets can be removed while mpv event callbacks are still active.
- Compare the current lifecycle guard comments to actual code paths used in production background transitions.

## Suggested fix direction

Possible areas to validate, not assumptions:

- Add a production lifecycle stop/pause path similar to the existing hot-reload emergency `stopAll()` if background transitions leave mpv callbacks alive.
- Ensure all media_kit stream subscriptions/listeners are cancelled before native player disposal.
- Ensure player disposal is awaited where the widget tree may otherwise tear down first.
- Add defensive guards around callbacks/listeners so stale native events cannot mutate disposed Dart state.

## Verification

- Add a focused pooled player lifecycle test for dispose/background order if possible.

title: fix(crashlytics): guard iOS video composition render size before AVPlayerItem assignment
body:
## Crashlytics evidence

Crashlytics issue: `23e8044843c5408cbb210460902dbfeb`

Console: https://console.firebase.google.com/project/openvine-co/crashlytics/app/ios:co.openvine.app/issues/23e8044843c5408cbb210460902dbfeb?&time=1776614940000:1777219740000

Window queried with Firebase MCP: `2026-04-19T16:09:00Z` to `2026-04-26T16:09:00Z`

Impact in that window:

- Events: 53
- Impacted users: 25
- Sessions: 53
- First seen: `1.0.9`
- Last seen: `1.0.9`
- Signal: fresh, first appeared 6 days before query

Sample event:

- Event: `projects/972941478875/apps/1:972941478875:ios:f61272b3cf485df244b5fe/events/9ca67ed88eb546af9893d71a2e181048_2211522001749315754`
- Event time: `2026-04-26T14:34:51Z`
- App version: `1.0.9 (660)`
- Device: iPhone 15 Pro Max, iOS `26.3.1`
- Breadcrumb path: welcome -> explore -> drafts -> video-editor-draft

Exception:

```text
NSInvalidArgumentException: *** -[AVPlayerItem setVideoComposition:] video composition must have a positive renderSize
at -[AVPlayerItem setVideoComposition:]
at closure #1 in DivineVideoPlayerInstance.handleSetClips(_:result:) (DivineVideoPlayerInstance.swift:140)
```

## Start here

Likely code path:

- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/ios/Classes/DivineVideoPlayerInstance.swift`
- `handleSetClips(_:result:)` creates `AVPlayerItem(asset: composition)` and immediately assigns `AVVideoComposition(propertiesOf: composition)`.
- `buildComposition(from:)` can return a composition where AVFoundation cannot infer a positive video render size, most likely from a bad/zero-size source track, invalid trim range, empty inserted video tracks, or metadata not loaded/validated before creating the video composition.

Relevant local lines at time of triage:

```text
DivineVideoPlayerInstance.swift:139  let playerItem = AVPlayerItem(asset: composition)
DivineVideoPlayerInstance.swift:140  playerItem.videoComposition = AVVideoComposition(propertiesOf: composition)
```

## Investigation requirements

Follow root-cause first. Do not just wrap this in `try?` and hide playback failures.

- Add or inspect diagnostics around every clip passed into `buildComposition`: URI, `startMs`, `endMs`, loaded video track count, natural size, preferred transform, duration, and computed trim range.
- Confirm whether the composition has at least one inserted video segment and a positive render size before assigning `videoComposition`.
- Handle invalid clips by returning a Flutter error to Dart rather than throwing an uncaught Objective-C exception.
- Check whether draft/editor reopen paths can pass stale or partially rendered clip files into the native player.
- Keep iOS and macOS implementations in sync if the same code exists under `macos/Classes`.

## Suggested fix direction

Validate the composition before `playerItem.videoComposition = ...`:

- Ensure at least one usable video track is inserted.
- Derive a positive render size from the source track natural size after applying preferred transform.
- Reject zero/NaN/negative dimensions and invalid trim ranges before constructing or assigning `AVVideoComposition`.
- Surface `COMPOSITION_ERROR` to Dart with enough context for Crashlytics breadcrumbs, without including user-private file paths.

## Verification

- Add focused tests or native-side validation coverage where practical for zero-size/invalid clip metadata.
- Run the relevant `divine_video_player` tests from `mobile/packages/divine_video_player`.
- Run app-level Flutter tests that exercise video editor draft/metadata preview flows if available.
- Manually verify reopening a draft and entering video metadata no longer crashes on iOS.
- After release, confirm Crashlytics issue `23e8044843c5408cbb210460902dbfeb` stops receiving events.

- Crashlytics issue d7f31dcbfb97da0bbf92d485de8b311b: FVPEventBridge.sendOrQueue, same FlutterEngine-not-run exception.
- Crashlytics issue 92facabdc6fe409a7daf9be134d23be5: FVPFrameUpdater.displayLinkFired, EXC_BAD_ACCESS while notifying textureFrameAvailable.
- Crashlytics issue 9a3f9d030c6aacc38b26a6472b6c84e7: VideoTextureOutput.deliverFrame(_:), EXC_BAD_ACCESS while notifying textureFrameAvailable.

These are all native callback/texture delivery paths continuing after the engine/player/texture recipient is no longer valid. Existing issues #3411 and #3416 cover adjacent media_kit/mpv and Android FlutterJNI crashes, but I did not find an exact iOS issue for these FVP/ProVideo texture/event callbacks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Native iOS event sinks check engine/channel readiness before posting progress/events.
- CADisplayLink, KVO, frame-output, and texture callbacks are stopped or deregistered before engine/player teardown.
- textureFrameAvailable is never called after the texture registry/engine has been invalidated.
- Add lifecycle regression coverage where practical; at minimum document the teardown ordering and verify with an iOS run that rapidly opens/closes editor/player surfaces.
- Keep this focused on native callback lifecycle; do not bundle unrelated Dart player refactors.

title: fix(crashlytics): snapshot relay pending messages before resend
body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows Relay.onConnected iterating a pending-message list while that list can be mutated.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue d631ee3d717e4100ece541806d6e8e1d: 1 nonfatal event, 1 user.
- Error: Concurrent modification during iteration: Instance(length:5) of '_GrowableList'.
- Stack: ListIterator.moveNext -> Relay.onConnected at mobile/packages/nostr_sdk/lib/relay/relay.dart:77.
- Code: Relay.onConnected iterates pendingMessages directly and clears it after the loop around lines 77-89. Sending/resubscribe work can mutate pendingMessages while the loop is active.

This is a small deterministic SDK bug and should be fixable without changing protocol behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- onConnected drains or snapshots pendingMessages before resending so mutations during send do not affect the active iteration.
- Preserve full Nostr payloads and subscription IDs; do not truncate IDs in code, logs, or tests.
- Add a nostr_sdk unit test that mutates/queues a pending message during reconnect and verifies no ConcurrentModificationError occurs.
- Preserve the intended behavior of replaying pending messages exactly once per reconnect.

title: Unified async VideoEvent resolver for deep-linkable edit/share routes
body:
The published-video edit route introduced in PR #4322 currently requires a VideoEvent passed via GoRouter extra and is intentionally not deep-linkable. This works for existing call sites because they already hold the full VideoEvent in memory, but it leaves /video-edit registered in the canonical route system without a resolvable ID-based entry point.

Why this needs follow-up:
- VideoEventService.getVideoById only searches feed caches and applies shouldHideVideo filtering, which can hide the user’s own non-Divine-hosted videos.
- PersonalEventCacheService.getEventById is scoped to the current user cache, returns Event?, and is unavailable until initialization completes.
- The current app has no unified async resolver that can load a VideoEvent for edit/share routes from cache, in-memory feed state, and relay/network fallback.

Scope:
- Build a unified async VideoEvent resolver across VideoEventService, PersonalEventCacheService, and relay fetch fallback.
- Relax shouldHideVideo for own-content edit paths so users can edit their own videos even when Divine-hosted-only filtering is enabled.

- Revisit route normalization and route-context handling once the route is actually reconstructable from URL state.

title: perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository
body:
## Summary
PR #4286 adds a read-time workaround in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart` to repair stale inbox preview data by overlaying each conversation row with the actual latest message from `direct_messages`.

That workaround fixes correctness, but it introduces a new performance problem: every emission from `watchAcceptedConversations()` and `watchPotentialRequests()` now performs one `DirectMessagesDao.getMessagesForConversation(..., limit: 1)` query per conversation.

For users with many conversations, this turns a single conversations-stream update into an N+1 fan-out of DAO reads.

## Current implementation
PR #4286 changes these paths:
- `watchAcceptedConversations()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`
- `watchPotentialRequests()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`

`_overlayLatestMessages()` then does:
- iterate every `ConversationRow`
- call `getMessagesForConversation(row.id, limit: 1, ownerPubkey: _ownerPubkey)`
- copy the latest message fields back onto the domain model
- resort the list in memory by the overlaid timestamp

Relevant code in the PR:
- `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart:1667-1698`

## Why this matters
The workaround runs on every stream tick, not just on first load.

That means:
- 10 conversations -> 10 extra DAO reads per emit
- 100 conversations -> 100 extra DAO reads per emit
- every accepted-conversations refresh and every potential-requests refresh pays this cost

Even if the reads are parallelized with `Future.wait`, the app still performs one query per conversation, plus an in-memory resort, on every update. This is avoidable read amplification on a hot inbox path.

## Root cause
The comment added in PR #4286 documents the underlying correctness problem well: the denormalized `conversations.lastMessageContent` / `lastMessageTimestamp` fields can drift out of sync with the real latest message in `direct_messages`.

The overlay is compensating for write-path drift at read time.

## Desired outcome
Keep the correctness fix, but remove the per-conversation query fan-out.

## Candidate fixes
### Option A: batched latest-message query
Add a DAO method that fetches the latest message for many conversation ids in one query, for example:
- `getLatestMessagesForConversations(List<String> conversationIds, {required String ownerPubkey})`

Then replace the N queries in `_overlayLatestMessages()` with a single batched read and a map/join in memory.

### Option B: fix denormalized-column drift at the write path
Investigate why `conversations.lastMessageContent` and `lastMessageTimestamp` become stale during backfill / out-of-order gift-wrap arrival.

If the write path can guarantee the denormalized columns always reflect the actual latest message, the overlay can be removed entirely and the existing conversation-watch queries can remain the source of truth.

### Option C: hybrid transition
Ship a batched DAO read first to remove the N+1 cost, then follow with a write-path correctness fix and delete the overlay once the denormalized columns are trustworthy again.

## Acceptance criteria
- Inbox conversation streams no longer perform one `getMessagesForConversation(... limit: 1)` call per conversation on every emit.
- The inbox preview still shows the true latest message even when the conversation row is stale.
- Ordering remains based on the real latest message timestamp.
- Existing regression coverage for stale preview overlay remains intact or is updated to cover the new batched/corrected implementation.
- If the final fix relies on transitional code, include a linked `TODO(#issue)` with a clear removal plan.

## Regression tests to preserve
The tests added in PR #4286 should remain conceptually covered:
- overlays the latest message from `DirectMessageRow` over the denormalized row preview
- re-sorts conversations by the actual latest message timestamp
- file-message preview overlay behavior

## Context
Introduced while reviewing PR #4286.

This issue tracks removing the new N+1 inbox read-path debt without losing the correctness fix that motivated it.

title: DM: surface swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures in self-wrap recovery paths
body:
## Summary

`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` swallow DAO bookkeeping failures via `Log.error` only. Crashlytics doesn't see them because the wrapped errors are not `Reportable` per `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. Today we have no signal for how often these doubly-degraded paths fire in production.

## Problem

The doubly-degraded path in `recoverSelfWrap` (publish landed; both `deleteById` and fallback `markSelfWrapStatus(sent)` threw) is documented as safe via NIP-17 receive-side dedup — but "safe" is hypothesis until we measure. Same for any DAO write failure inside the recipient-success finalize path. We currently have no way to know if this is happening 0/day or 100/day.

## Desired Outcome

Surface DAO bookkeeping failures in these recovery paths so they're visible in monitoring without flooding Crashlytics.

## Scope

Decide between:

1. **Wrap as `Reportable`** per the matrix in `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. These are arguably "programming-invariant violations" once the publish has landed — the row should always be writeable. Risk: Crashlytics noise on transient SQLite contention.
2. **Counter / debug surface only.** Increment a metric, expose under a debug screen. Less noisy, but invisible without proactive checking.
3. **Both.** Counter for triage, `Reportable` only on persistent runs (e.g., N consecutive failures for the same rumor).

## Context

- Two specific call sites today, both in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart`: `recoverSelfWrap` doubly-degraded catch, plus any throw inside `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` (currently upstream of any try/catch on the caller side).
- Spotted during PR #4106 review by Liz; follow-up to #4102.

title: epic(dm): reliability hardening
body:
## Summary

Forward-looking durability work for direct messaging, surfaced during
the investigation of #3902 ("looks sent, then disappeared"). The
user-visible symptom is closed by #3908. This Epic covers the deeper
reliability gaps that surface as separate UX problems on flaky
networks, slow remote signers (Keycast RPC), and second-device login
flows.

## Scope

### 1. Durable outgoing-message queue (#3909)

Outgoing DMs currently live only in `ConversationBloc` memory between
`emit(optimistic)` and the `_dmRepository.sendMessage` round-trip. App
kill, screen lock, or backgrounding mid-send loses the in-flight
attempt. There's no automatic retry on connectivity restore either —
only the SnackBar's manual button shipped in #3908.

A DB-backed `outgoing_dms` Drift table (#3911) + repository-level send
rewire + connectivity-driven retry service make sends durable across
session, app kill, and reinstall. UX surface: per-bubble delivery
indicator with retry / cancel actions.

### 2. Self-wrap publish failure detection (#3909, F3 in the investigation)

NIP-17 sends are two independent kind-1059 publishes (recipient gift
wrap + self-addressed gift wrap). The self-wrap failure was silently
swallowed at `nip17_message_service.dart:118-132`, so the recipient
could receive a message the sender's other devices would never see.

Surfaced via `NIP17SendResult.selfWrapPublished` in #3910, acted on by
the queue work — the row stays in `outgoing_dms` until both wraps
land, retried independently so the recipient is never double-delivered.

### 3. Future hardening (out of scope for current children, listed for visibility)

- NIP-04 fallback failure detection / retry. `_sendNip04Message` is
  fire-and-forget; a relay-side rejection of the legacy copy is
  invisible today.
- Group-DM partial-delivery UX. The same recipient-vs-self split
  applies per-participant for groups; failures on a subset need a
  per-recipient status indicator.
- Self-wrap retry telemetry / Crashlytics counters for triaging
  "messages disappeared" reports proactively rather than via Zendesk.

## Consolidates

| Issue / PR | Title | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #3902 | fix: Inconvenience with sending a recieveing DMs (Zendesk) | Closed |
| #3908 | fix(dm): clear optimistic on send failure, surface retry, key bloc on repo identity | Merged |
| #3909 | task(dm): durable outgoing-message queue + self-wrap publish failure detection | Open (sub-issue of this Epic) |
| #3910 | fix(dm): surface NIP-17 self-wrap publish failure via NIP17SendResult | Merged |
| #3911 | feat(db): add outgoing_dms Drift table + DAO for durable DM queue | Merged |
| #4106 | feat(dm): self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial sends | Merged |
| #4241 | feat(dm): auto-sweep self-wrap-failed outgoing_dms via foreground retry service | Merged |
| #4240 | DM: add recoverFullSend primitive for recipient-wrap-failed outgoing_dms rows | Open |
| #4127 | DM: surface swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures in self-wrap recovery paths | Open |
| #4296 | perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository | Open |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An outgoing DM survives the app being killed mid-send and reaches the relay automatically when connectivity returns.
- [ ] A DM whose recipient wrap succeeded but self wrap failed is visibly distinguished in the conversation, with a recoverable action that re-attempts only the missing publish — never re-publishes to the recipient.
- [ ] No silent self-wrap failure path remains in `NIP17MessageService`.
- [ ] Existing-install upgrade is non-destructive: the new `outgoing_dms` table appears via runtime `_createMissingTables`, not a schema-version bump.
- [ ] All work in scope ships behind tests that pin the partial-delivery state, the retry round-trip, and multi-account isolation.

## In-repo precedents to mirror

- `PendingActions` table + `PendingActionService` (`mobile/lib/services/pending_action_service.dart`) — durable retry queue for likes / reposts / follows. Same retry-config defaults: 5 retries, 2 s → 5 min, 2× backoff.
- `UploadManager` (`mobile/lib/services/upload_manager.dart`) — durable persistence + retry for video uploads.
- `_PooledVideoFeedItem` (`mobile/lib/screens/feed/video_feed_page.dart:911-942`) — `BlocProvider` keyed on Riverpod-provided dependency identity, mirrored in #3908 for `ConversationPage`.

## Additional Open Follow-up Work

- #4240 — recipient-wrap-failed outgoing_dms recovery primitive
- #4127 — monitoring / reporting for swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures in recovery paths
- #4296 — inbox latest-message overlay N+1 performance cleanup

title: task(dm): durable outgoing-message queue + self-wrap publish failure detection
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3902 (fixed in #3908). PR #3908 shipped the immediate user-visible fix (clear optimistic on failure, retry SnackBar, BlocProvider keyed on repo identity). Two durability gaps remain and they're the same problem at different layers — file together so the design covers both:

- **C — Durable outgoing-message queue.** In-flight sends only live in `ConversationBloc` memory. Background the app, lock the screen, or pop the conversation while a send is in flight, and the optimistic + the in-flight `await sendMessage` are both lost. There's also no automatic retry on connectivity restoration — only the SnackBar's one-tap manual retry.
- **F3 — Silent self-wrap publish failure** at `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/nip17_message_service.dart:118-132`:
  ```dart
  if (selfWrapEvent != null) {
    await _nostrService.publishEvent(selfWrapEvent);  // result discarded
  }
  ```
  The recipient's gift wrap can publish successfully while the self-addressed wrap silently fails to land. Recipient sees the message; sender's other devices never see it. The current test at `nip17_message_service_test.dart:223` (`returns success even when self-wrap publish throws`) literally pins that bug.

## Why one issue, not two

C is the *durability* layer. F3 is the trigger that makes durability necessary. Without C, F3 has nowhere to surface the partial-failure state to the user. Without F3, C can't tell "fully delivered" from "delivered to recipient only" — which is the difference between deleting the queue row and keeping it for retry.

## Proposed approach (high level)

Mirror the in-repo `PendingActions` / `PendingActionService` precedent (`mobile/packages/db_client/lib/src/database/tables.dart:361` and `mobile/lib/services/pending_action_service.dart`):

- New `outgoing_dms` Drift table — pending-queue row per outgoing rumor with **independent** `recipient_wrap_status` and `self_wrap_status` columns (each enum: pending | sent | failed), `retry_count`, `last_error`, `last_attempt_at`, `owner_pubkey`, `rumor_event_json`. Storing the rumor JSON keeps the rumor id stable across retries — critical for receiver-side dedup.
- `NIP17MessageService.sendPrivateMessage` returns per-wrap status instead of a single bool — surfaces F3.
- `DmRepository.sendMessage` inserts the queue row first, calls the service, updates the row with both statuses; on both-success deletes queue row + inserts `direct_messages` atomically; on either-failure retains the row.
- New `OutgoingDmRetryService` — `PendingActionService`-shaped, listens to connectivity, replays failed rows with exponential backoff (steal `PendingActionRetryConfig` defaults: 5 retries, 2s → 5min, 2× backoff).
- `ConversationBloc` switches to `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)`. State carries a `Map<String, MessageDeliveryStatus>` keyed by rumor id — the existing `state.messages` list is unchanged in shape, status flows through a parallel map (avoids polluting `DmMessage` with delivery state, keeps `state_management.md` rules intact).
- `MessageBubble` renders WhatsApp-style indicators (clock / single check / double check / error / cancelled). Long-press on failed surfaces Retry + Cancel actions in the existing `MessageActionsSheet`.

The existing `lastFailedSend` SnackBar from PR #3908 stays as the synchronous "fail-fast retry while the input is still in your head" affordance. The queue handles the asynchronous "eventually failed or partially succeeded, recoverable later" cases. Both can fire on the same failure — tests pin the no-double-publish invariant.

## Architecture, files, tests, risks

Full plan with bottom-up implementation order (Client → Repo → Service → BLoC → UI), affected-files table, layer-by-layer test strategy, and a risks section (rumor id stability across retries, half-delivered UX, backoff tuning, multi-account isolation, schema-version-1 + `_createMissingTables` upgrade path) is in the PR thread on #3908. Will be moved here when the work begins.

## Out of scope

- **Approach D** from the original investigation (split persisted vs. optimistic into separate state fields). Once C ships, the queue's per-row status IS the principled split — D folds into C for free.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An outgoing DM survives the app being killed mid-send and reaches the relay automatically when connectivity returns.
- [ ] A DM whose recipient wrap succeeded but self wrap failed is visibly distinguished in the conversation, with a recoverable action that re-attempts only the missing publish (no double-deliver to the recipient).
- [ ] All existing #3908 tests + bloc + view tests stay green.
- [ ] New tests (DAO, repo, service, bloc, view, migration) cover the matrix above.
- [ ] No regression in the SnackBar retry flow shipped by #3908.

## References

- Original Zendesk-imported bug: #3902 ("Inconvenience with sending and receiving DMs")
- Immediate fix: #3908
- In-repo precedent: `PendingActions` table + `PendingActionService` (likes/reposts/follows offline queue)
- Self-wrap site: `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/nip17_message_service.dart:118-132`
- NIP-17 spec: gift wrap (kind 1059) → seal (kind 13) → rumor (kind 14/15)

title: fix(search): drop idle placeholder on Explore → Search with prefilled query
body:
## Summary

Tapping into Explore's search bar and typing 2+ characters auto-pushes `/search-results/:query` after a 300ms debounce. The destination then flashed **"Enter a search query / Discover something interesting"** for another ~300–600ms before BLoCs were dispatched and section skeletons appeared. On slow networks the window stretched, reading as a flash, error, or hang. This PR makes the destination drop the idle placeholder when a route arg query is pending, and dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously on AppBar mount so the BLoCs advance from `initial` this same frame.

Closes #3802. Companion to parent epic #3801.

## Root cause

`SearchResultsView` keyed the idle short-circuit on `VideoSearchBloc.state.status == initial` alone. That signal correctly identifies "no query entered" (the load-bearing PR #3199 fix for #3023's infinite skeleton) but does NOT distinguish it from "query just arrived as a route arg, AppBar dispatch is still pending its 300ms UI debounce."

## Changes

- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_view.dart` — add optional `String initialQuery = ''`. Gate the idle short-circuit on `initialQuery.trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so it matches the BLoC handlers' own gate exactly. Falls through to sections (whose own skeletons render on `initial || loading/searching` with empty results) when a searchable query is pending. Inline comment cites PR #3199 / #3023 so a future reader doesn't simplify the conditional back to the buggy form.
- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_page.dart` — pass `initialQuery` from `_SearchResultsBody` to `SearchResultsView` (1 line).
- `lib/screens/search_results/widgets/search_results_app_bar.dart` — reorder `initState` so the controller text is seeded BEFORE the listener is attached. When `initialQuery.isNotEmpty`, dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously to all four BLoCs. The BLoCs' `debounceRestartable` still applies; same-query dedup guards coalesce any late-arriving event. Focus model intentionally untouched — that's sibling issue #3020 / #3803 territory.

All 5 entry points to `SearchResultsPage` go through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: query)` (Explore auto-push, `@mention` link tap, universal link, deep link, GoRoute), so this fix applies uniformly.

### Commit history

1. `1f99c2b6` — initial fix.
2. `2407333d` — self-review follow-up: tighten the view's idle gate from `isEmpty` to `trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so reachable edge cases (whitespace-only or 1-char deep links like `/search-results/a` and `/search-results/%20%20`) don't render infinite skeletons (a #3023-class regression in the corner). Two extra regression tests pin the corrected behavior.

## Scope clarification

Per the issue body: "Do not collapse this issue into keyboard/focus behavior. They are related, but not identical." This PR is scoped to the intermediate-state symptom only. The focus and keyboard work belongs to:

- #3020 — keyboard collapses (assigned to @untreu2)
- #3803 — canonical focus behavior (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz)

The parent epic #3801 calls for these three children to land as one cohesive transition PR (Gate 2). I scoped this PR to #3802 alone; bundling is the epic driver's call.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/screens/search_results/` → **85 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/{video,user,hashtag,list}_search test/blocs/search_results_filter` → **119 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/explore_screen_pure_test.dart` → 12 passing
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- [x] `dart format` → clean

New test coverage:
- `search_results_view_test.dart` — new `with non-empty initialQuery` group asserts `SearchSectionInitialState` does NOT render when `initialQuery` is non-empty + status is initial, and that the all-filter section list renders instead. Plus two regression tests pinning the whitespace-only and sub-min-length cases to the idle placeholder (cures the #3023-class edge case).
- `search_results_app_bar_test.dart` — adds missing `_MockListSearchBloc` mock (the existing setUp had a gap), plus three new tests: synchronous dispatch on non-empty `initialQuery`, NO dispatch on empty `initialQuery`, and no double-dispatch after the 300ms debounce window elapses.
- Existing idle-state tests preserved verbatim — PR #3199's load-bearing behavior is unchanged for the empty-query path.

## Manual device testing guide

### What changed (one-paragraph context for QA)

When you typed 2+ characters in Explore's search bar and the app auto-pushed to `/search-results/:query`, you saw a brief "Enter a search query / Discover something interesting" placeholder for ~300–600ms before search results loaded — especially noticeable on slow networks. After this fix, the destination shows section skeletons immediately and lands on real results once they arrive. The empty-query case (opening the search screen directly) still shows the "Enter a search query" placeholder as before.

### Build

Pick one:

- **Preview web build** (fastest, no local setup): open the `Mobile PR Preview` link from this PR's checks. The bot posts a `https://<hash>.openvine-app.pages.dev` URL on every push.
- **Local install** on the device:
  ```bash
  git fetch origin
  git checkout fix/3802-search-intermediate-state
  cd mobile
  flutter pub get
  flutter run --release   # release matters — debug mode is slower and masks the symptom
  ```
- **TestFlight / internal build** if one is cut later — pull the build tagged with this PR's SHA.

Notes:
- The bug is more visible in `release` than `debug` (debug is slow anyway, so any flash is harder to attribute).
- The bug is most visible on slow networks. Throttle to "Slow 3G" via iOS Settings → Developer → Network Link Conditioner (or Android Developer Options → Networking → Network type → "GPRS"), or use a proxy throttle.

### Golden path — primary repro from issue #3802

1. Launch the app. Sign in if needed.
2. Tap the **Explore** bottom-nav tab.
3. Tap the search bar at the top of Explore.
4. Type `hello` (or any 2+ character query). **Stop typing** and wait.
5. After ~300ms the app navigates to the search results screen.

What to look for (frame-by-frame):

| Frame | Before this fix (broken) | After this fix (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation completes | Screen renders with a centered search icon + **"Enter a search query"** + **"Discover something interesting"** | Screen renders with shimmer **skeletons** for People / Lists / Tags / Videos sections |
| ~300–600ms later | Skeletons appear (the placeholder fades) | (same skeletons continue, no flash transition) |
| Results arrive | Real results render | Real results render |

- **Pass criteria**: at no point during the transition does the "Enter a search query" copy appear.
- **Fail signal**: if you see "Enter a search query" or "Discover something interesting" even briefly, the fix didn't apply.

Tip: if you can't catch it visually, screen-record at 60 fps and step through frames.

### Slow-network case — the issue's "feels like a hang" complaint

Same steps as Golden path, but throttle to Slow 3G first.

- **Pass**: skeletons hold for as long as the network needs, then results land. No misleading "Enter a query" text. No fallback to an error state until/unless results genuinely fail.
- **Fail**: the "Enter a search query" copy appears, OR the screen looks empty/blank for any period.

### Direct entry to /search-results (regression check for #3023 — DO NOT skip)

This is the load-bearing case from PR #3199. **This must still work the OLD way.**

Two ways to trigger:

A. Universal/deep link with empty query — open the app from a `divine.video/search-results/` link (no query) if you can construct one, OR

B. In the running app: Explore → tap search bar → land on `/search-results/` with no query in the field.

- **Pass**: centered "Enter a search query" / "Discover something interesting" placeholder renders. **This is correct** — it was the #3023 fix.
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely (that's #3023 reopening).

### Edge cases — sub-min-length & whitespace-only query (the F1 finding addressed in commit 2)

Reachable via deep / universal links — try if you can construct them, otherwise skip:

1. Open `divine.video/search-results/a` (single character) — or build a URL pointing at `/search-results/a` and open it from another app.
2. Open `divine.video/search-results/%20%20%20` (whitespace-only, URL-encoded).

- **Pass for both**: idle placeholder "Enter a search query" renders. (BLoCs gate on `length >= 2` so sub-min queries never reach the network; the view correctly treats them as idle.)
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely.

### Other entry paths — same expected behavior

These all converge through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: ...)` so they should all behave consistently:

1. Tap an `@username` mention in a comment (links via `linkified_text`) — should land on search with the username pre-filled, **no misleading placeholder**.
2. Open the app from a universal link `https://divine.video/search-results/<query>` — same.
3. Open from a push-notification deep link with a search term — same.

- **Pass**: skeletons + results. No "Enter a search query" flash.

### Focus / keyboard — explicitly NOT in scope here

This fix does NOT change focus or keyboard behavior. Those are tracked separately in:
- **#3020** (keyboard collapses when typing in Explore → search page) — assigned to @untreu2
- **#3803** (canonical focus model) — assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz

For #3802 QA: **don't flag** keyboard or focus issues against this PR. The destination field will not auto-focus when navigated with a pre-filled query — that's the existing behavior and intentionally untouched.

### Filters & deep search — confirm nothing else regressed

1. Land on `/search-results/hello` (golden path).
2. Tap the **filter pill** (top-right). Switch between All / People / Videos / Tags / Lists.

- **Pass**: each filter renders its skeletons → results. No "Enter a search query" appears on any filter tab even before results arrive.
- **Fail**: any filter renders the empty-query placeholder.

### Empty results — make sure we don't show idle instead of empty

1. Search a query with truly no results (e.g. random keyboard mash like `xqzqzqzq`).
2. Wait for results to settle (~1–5 seconds).

- **Pass**: each section shows its appropriate empty-state ("No results found for X" / "Try a different search term"). **Not** "Enter a search query."
- **Fail**: the idle placeholder shows after BLoCs have completed.

### Error/timeout (people search) — confirm degraded-empty UI

Same as above on a flaky network. If NIP-50 user search times out:

- **Pass**: People section shows the retry affordance (per the #3791 / #3804 fix that already landed). Other sections show their results or empty states.
- **Fail**: idle placeholder shows instead of the retry UI.

### Sign-off checklist

```
[ ] Golden path: type `hello` in Explore, no "Enter a search query" flash
[ ] Slow-3G repro: same, with throttle on
[ ] Direct-entry (empty query): "Enter a search query" placeholder DOES render
[ ] Sub-min-length deep link `/search-results/a`: idle placeholder renders
[ ] Whitespace-only deep link `/search-results/%20%20`: idle placeholder renders
[ ] @mention tap → search: skeletons not placeholder
[ ] Universal link with query: skeletons not placeholder
[ ] Filter switch: each filter shows skeletons until results, never placeholder
[ ] Empty result (mash query): empty-state not placeholder
```

title: feat(cache_sync): account-scoped invalidation
body:
## Description

Foundation PR for the data-foundation epic (#4335). `cache_sync` gains **account-scoped invalidation** and `AuthService.signOut` consolidates cache invalidation onto it:

- `CacheSync.invalidatePrefix(prefix)` clears every entry whose key starts with `prefix`. Cache keys follow the `${pubkey}:operation` convention (RFC #4244), so calling with the leaving account's pubkey hex wipes only that account and leaves other accounts on the same device intact. SQL `LIKE` metacharacters (`%`, `_`, `\`) in `prefix` are escaped via `LIKE ... ESCAPE '\'` so the match is literal.
- Empty `prefix` now throws `ArgumentError` in all builds. The guard is runtime-enforced, so the empty-string path cannot degrade to a full-wipe in release.
- `follow_repository`'s four cache-key helpers move from the legacy `operation_${pubkey}` shape to RFC #4244's `${pubkey}:operation` shape so the new prefix invalidation actually matches.
- `AuthService.signOut` now owns cache invalidation. It captures the current pubkey and calls `CacheSync.invalidatePrefix(currentPubkey)` on **both** destructive and non-destructive paths. Invalidation failure is forwarded to Crashlytics via the existing `_reportStorageError` path so a silent disk-residency regression is observable, but the sign-out flow remains failure-tolerant.
- `SettingsAccountCubit` loses its `CacheSync.invalidateAll()` calls and `cache_sync` import. The cubit returns to single-responsibility account-list orchestration.
- The now-unused `CacheSync.invalidateAll()` / `CacheDao.deleteAll()` surface is removed rather than left as dead API.
- Small `@visibleForTesting void debugSetCurrentKeyContainer(...)` seam added to `AuthService` so the multi-account assertion test can exercise the authenticated path without driving the full sign-in pipeline.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4360. Parent epic #4335. RFC #4244. Original `cache_sync` introduction #4251.

title: chore: Gate Nostr side effects on session readiness
body:
## Description

Users could lose push registration on cold launch because auth could be ready before Nostr could sign yet.
This change separates identity readiness from Nostr readiness and makes signer-dependent work wait for the matching ready client.
That matters because push registration, notification preferences, and blocklist sync all publish Nostr events.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3929

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Summary

Auth state now means the app knows who the user is.
It no longer means the Nostr client is ready to sign and publish.
The app now waits for an explicit ready session before running side effects that need the signer.

## What Changed

The flow now carries the ready pubkey and client together.
Work that publishes through Nostr rejects stale sessions and queues preferences until the matching session is ready.
Sign-out also runs outgoing push deregistration before signer teardown.

- Added `NostrSessionReadiness` and kept `isNostrReadyProvider` as a compatibility shim.
- Moved push registration, token refresh, preference publishing, push deregistration, and blocklist sync to ready-session or pre-teardown paths.
- Added warning-only wrappers so non-critical push publish failures do not escape async listeners.
- Added regression tests for cold launch, account switch, teardown ordering, queued preferences, and async error handling.

## Testing

I rebased onto latest `origin/main` and ran the full Flutter checks.
The analyzer found no issues, and the full test suite passed with 8,383 passing tests and 400 skipped tests.

- `git fetch https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile.git main:refs/remotes/origin/main && git rebase origin/main`
- `flutter analyze`
- `flutter test`

## Risks

The main risk is lifecycle ordering around sign-out and account switch.
The new tests cover the flows that could use a stale or placeholder Nostr client.
Identity-only listeners such as routing and Zendesk still use auth state.

title: fix(push): NIP-44 token registration races Nostr signer readiness on cold start
body:
## Summary

`pushNotificationSync` (`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart:1178-1219`) fires `pushService.register(pubkey)` as soon as `authState` becomes `authenticated`. That moment is **before** the Nostr signer is fully ready — particularly for OAuth/Keycast users — so `nip44Encrypt` returns `null`, the token registration aborts silently, and the device misses push notifications until the next FCM token refresh (which may not happen for hours/days).

This is one of the failures observed in DollyAnna's logs on #3862, but it has no causal relationship to the upload 503 reported in that issue. Filing here so the push-side fix can be tracked independently and tied to the right user-impacting symptom.

## Repro signal

In the user logs from #3862:

```
[2026-05-02T19:20:25.644052] [WARNING] [VIDEO] (VideoEventService) Cannot subscribe - Nostr service not initialized (will retry when ready)
[2026-05-02T19:20:26.077041] [ERROR] [SYSTEM] (PushNotificationService) NIP-44 encryption failed for token registration
```

The encryption-failed line fires ~1.4s after Nostr is logged as not yet initialized; subsequent successful Nostr operations (e.g. NIP-98 token signing at `19:20:34`) confirm the signer becomes available shortly afterward.

## Root cause

`KeycastNostrIdentity.nip44Encrypt` (`mobile/lib/services/nostr_identity.dart:189-195`) tries the local signer first; `LocalKeySigner.nip44Encrypt` (`mobile/lib/services/local_key_signer.dart:134-151`) returns `null` when `_keyContainer == null`. It then falls through to the RPC signer, which also returns `null` if Keycast RPC isn't yet connected. Both paths failing produces the observed `NIP-44 encryption failed for token registration` log line, and `_publishRegistration` aborts without publishing the kind-3079 event.

`pushNotificationSync` watches `authServiceProvider` and fires `register(pubkey)` on the first `AuthState.authenticated` emission. There's no readiness gate equivalent to `isNostrReadyProvider` — which other features already use (`profileRepositoryProvider`, `pendingActionServiceProvider` per `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart:1110-1135`).

## Suggested fix shape

Gate `register()` behind `isNostrReadyProvider` using the same Pattern A as `profileRepositoryProvider`. Either:

1. Wait inside `pushNotificationSync` for `isNostrReadyProvider` to flip true before calling `register()`, or
2. Have `PushNotificationService.register()` itself wait on the readiness signal (cleaner, single-responsibility).

A retry-on-null shim inside `_publishRegistration` would also work but would be less principled — the right answer is to not call into the signer until the signer is ready.

## Why this is _not_ a fix for #3862

The original triage on #3862 hypothesised that the same NIP-44 encryption failure caused the profile-picture upload 503. That hypothesis is incorrect:

- Profile-picture upload uses **kind 24242** BUD-01 **signed** events (`mobile/packages/blossom_upload_service/lib/src/blossom_upload_service.dart:255-333`). It does not call `nip44Encrypt` at any point.
- NIP-44 in this app is only used by `PushNotificationService` (kinds 3079, 3080, 3083 — token registration, deregistration, preferences updates).

The signed-event path was working fine in DollyAnna's same log window: `Event signed and validated: 29b02969e7b56ad96e157ba6a6b981d55c93f0350ba50889e2b33385abdfc49f` at 19:20:34. The two failures happened to co-occur but are independent.

## Relationship to existing issues

- **Linked**: #3743 (push notifications). This is the matching user-visible symptom of the same race.
- **Not linked**: #3862 (profile-picture upload), #3858 (account deletion), #3161 (username), #3271 (video deletion). The original triage clustering proposed these as a "NIP-44 cluster" — none of those code paths use NIP-44 encryption, so a fix here won't change their behaviour.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pushService.register()` does not run until the signer can produce non-null NIP-44 ciphertext
- [ ] Test asserting that on cold-start with signer-not-ready, `register()` does not call `_nostrClient.publishEvent` until readiness is established
- [ ] Crashlytics no longer shows `NIP-44 encryption failed for token registration` from a freshly-installed-and-launched app

title: task(cache_sync): add MigrationStrategy + schema-versioned wipe for legacy key residue
body:
## Description

Follow-up debt cleanup for `cache_sync` after PR #4361.

`cache_sync` currently has a short-lived cohort of legacy keys written in the old `operation_${pubkey}` shape from the 3-day window after `cache_sync` shipped in #4251 and before RFC #4244 key-shape migration landed in #4361. Those rows are not reachable by `invalidatePrefix(currentPubkey)` because they do not start with the pubkey.

This issue tracks the correct cleanup instead of leaving the residue as an untracked follow-up:

- add `cache_sync` migration/versioning scaffolding (`MigrationStrategy` / `onUpgrade` path)
- perform a schema-versioned wipe or equivalent one-time cleanup for legacy `operation_${pubkey}` cache rows
- make the cleanup explicit and reproducible rather than relying on eventual LRU eviction

## Why

PR #4361 intentionally shipped account-scoped invalidation without bundling schema-versioning work into the same diff. That scope cut is reasonable, but under the repo standard the deferred debt must be concretely tracked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cache_sync` has an explicit migration/versioning path for future schema bumps
- the legacy `operation_${pubkey}` cache-key cohort is removed by a deterministic upgrade path
- the implementation is documented in code/tests well enough that future cache-key migrations are straightforward
- all generated outputs and affected tests are updated as needed

## Related

- Parent epic: #4335
- Task issue: #4360
- Implementing PR: #4361
- Original cache_sync introduction: #4251

title: fix(security): strip BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth wire (#3359)
body:
## Description

Phase 1 emergency block for #3359 — strips the user's nsec from the
Keycast OAuth registration wire on both channels:

- `body['nsec']` field in `POST /api/headless/register`
- `<random>.<nsec1...>` suffix embedded in the PKCE `code_verifier`
  (later POSTed as `code_verifier` to `/api/oauth/token`)

The fix removes the parameters from the `keycast_flutter` package API
entirely so a future caller cannot re-introduce the leak. A POSIX-grep
CI guard locks the rule in.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3359

**Cross-repo coordination:** divinevideo/keycast#197 tracks the
server-side proof-of-possession redesign that Phase 2 depends on.
This PR ships **without** preserving BYOK identity binding — that is
restored once Phase 2 lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ❌ Breaking change (the public `KeycastOAuth.headlessRegister` and `KeycastOAuth.getAuthorizationUrl` APIs no longer accept `nsec` — intentional, for security)

## Trade-off

Until Phase 2 ships, BYOK secure-account upgrades fall through to the
server's auto-generate path. The user's existing local pubkey identity
is **not preserved** across the upgrade, but the local nsec stays
on-device and never crosses the network. This is the intentional
emergency-block trade-off — stop the leak today, restore identity
preservation in Phase 2 (depends on divinevideo/keycast#197).

## What's in this PR

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/pkce.dart` | `generateVerifier` no longer takes `nsec`; verifier is always pure-random base64url |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/lib/src/oauth/oauth_client.dart` | `getAuthorizationUrl` & `headlessRegister` drop `nsec`/`byokPubkey` parameters; `body['nsec']` removed; `byok_pubkey` URL param removed |
| `mobile/packages/keycast_flutter/test/{pkce,oauth_client}_test.dart` | Leak-as-feature tests flipped to negative regression guards |
| `mobile/lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart` | `load()` discards any persisted verifier containing `.nsec1` and clears storage (defense-in-depth migration) |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart` | Error log no longer interpolates `_pendingVerifier` value |
| `mobile/lib/screens/auth/secure_account_screen.dart` | Removed `authService.exportNsec()` and the `nsec:` arg |
| `mobile/test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart` | **New** — three tests for the migration |
| `mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` | **New** — POSIX-grep guard for production code |
| `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` | New `nsec-leak-guard` job |
| `mobile/integration_test/auth/session_expired_banner_test.dart` | `markTestSkipped` until Phase 2 — depends on BYOK preservation |

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test packages/keycast_flutter/{lib,test}` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test packages/keycast_flutter/` — 167/167 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/services/pending_verification_service_test.dart test/screens/auth/secure_account_screen_test.dart test/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit_test.dart` — 38/38 passing
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/divine_auth/` — 64/64 passing (regression-safety on the path that never carried nsec)
- [x] `bash mobile/tools/ci/grep_for_nsec_payload.sh` — exits 0 on this branch
- [x] Guard regex verified: matches `body['nsec']` + `'nsec':`; ignores `containsKey('nsec')` + `any(named: 'nsec')`
- [ ] Manual: e2e secure-account upgrade flow on a local dev stack (post-merge or staging)
- [ ] Coordinate with infra/security on retention review for any pre-fix request bodies that infra-layer components may have captured (separate workstream)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

title: fix: add sexual-content alias to _normalizeModerationLabel
body:
## summary

`_normalizeModerationLabel` in `video_stats.dart` normalizes server-emitted `sexual content` (with space) to `sexual-content` (with hyphen), but the switch statement has no alias mapping `sexual-content` to `sexual`. `ContentLabel.fromValue('sexual-content')` returns null.

the conservative unknown-label guard (added in #4365, already present in `nsfw_content_filter.dart`) correctly hides these videos. but it also means users who have explicitly set their `sexual` content preference to `show` still get force-hidden, since the label never resolves to `ContentLabel.sexual`.

## fix

one-liner in `mobile/packages/models/lib/src/video_stats.dart`:

```dart
case 'sexual-content':
  return 'sexual';
```

## context

surfaced during review of #4365. related to #4364 (conservative label tracking).

title: Track linkify user content render gaps across preview, list, and profile surfaces
body:
## Problem
Several user-visible text surfaces were rendering raw Nostr references instead of the resolved, linkified output already used elsewhere in the app. The affected gaps were inconsistent with adjacent UI and caused preview mode to diverge from real feed rendering.

## User Impact
- Curated list descriptions could show raw `nostr:npub...` references instead of resolved profile labels.
- Profile text comments could show plain text without clickable/linkified Nostr references.
- Video metadata preview mode could drop the description entirely and misuse the title field, which prevented preview rendering from matching the feed path.

## Scope
This tracking issue covers the bugfix shipped in PR #4358:
- switch curated list descriptions to shared `LinkifiedText` rendering
- switch profile text comments to shared clickable/linkified text rendering
- map video metadata preview `title` and `description` into the same `VideoEvent` fields used by real feed rendering
- add regression coverage for these surfaces

## Acceptance Criteria
- Curated list descriptions resolve and render Nostr profile references consistently with other linkified text surfaces.
- Profile text comments resolve and render Nostr profile references consistently with comment/feed surfaces.
- Video metadata preview renders description content through the same display path used by real videos.
- Regression tests cover all three touched surfaces.
- No new theming or test-helper debt is introduced in the touched files.

title: fix(safety): align profile feed moderation filtering with conservative unknown-ML-label behavior
body:
## Summary
PR #4350 fixed adult-content playback settings migration, but it left the profile-feed moderation path less strict than the repository/feed NSFW filter path.

Rabble called this out during review: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4350#issuecomment-4447083038

## Problem
`ProfileFeed` fetches videos and filters them through `VideoEventService.filterVideoList`, which still checks `video.moderationLabels` via `ContentFilterService.getPreferenceForLabels(modLabels)`. Unknown ML/server moderation labels fall back to `show`, so unrecognized labels can pass through.

Relevant code:
- `mobile/lib/providers/profile_feed_provider.dart:394`
- `mobile/lib/services/video_event_service.dart:633`
- `mobile/lib/services/video_event_service.dart:687`
- `mobile/lib/services/content_filter_service.dart:179`

By contrast, `createNsfwFilter` already applies the safer behavior: unknown ML moderation labels force-hide.

Reference path:
- `mobile/lib/services/nsfw_content_filter.dart:42`
- `mobile/test/services/nsfw_content_filter_test.dart:329`

## User impact
This can leave a moderation hole on profile feeds. Example from Rabble: Funnelcake/model tests already normalize `"sexual content"` to `"sexual-content"`, while the client enum recognizes `sexual`, not `sexual-content`, so suggestive/twerking content can still appear on profile feeds even when adult categories are locked to hide.

## Required fix
Make `VideoEventService.filterVideoList` match the conservative ML-label hide behavior already used by `createNsfwFilter` for unknown `video.moderationLabels`.

## Required tests
Add regression coverage on the `filterVideoList` path for at least:
- `moderationLabels: ['sexual-content']`
- another unknown ML/server moderation label

The fix is not complete until the profile-feed path and the repository/feed filter path are behaviorally aligned.

title: epic(data-foundation): unify caching, persistence, and platform dependency strategy
body:
## Summary

Caching, persistence, and platform dependency choices are currently fragmented across multiple storage backends, cache policies, and ownership models. This should be tracked as one coordinated foundation epic instead of several disconnected discussion issues.

This issue is the source of truth for data foundation work around caching, persistence, storage strategy, and shared dependency ownership.

## Problem

Current problems include:
- multiple cache systems with different TTL and invalidation rules
- overlapping persistent storage backends
- unclear ownership of platform/dependency decisions
- weak consistency around schema/versioning and long-term storage strategy
- difficulty answering basic questions about eviction, corruption recovery, or low-storage behavior

## Scope

- define cache tiers and invalidation strategy
- clarify persistent storage direction and migration strategy
- improve schema/versioning expectations
- document or reduce ad hoc dependency/platform decisions
- reduce duplicated “local solution per feature” patterns where a shared strategy is warranted

## Existing Related Work

- `#3624`
- `#3618`
- `#3657`
- `#3635`
- `#3629`
- `#3660`

## Acceptance Criteria

- caching and persistence work is grouped under a coherent parent issue
- the repo has an explicit direction for storage and cache policy
- dependency/platform ownership questions are no longer floating as unrelated audit leaves
- related leaf issues can be closed or superseded into this epic

## Done When

- data foundation work is coordinated instead of fragmented
- storage/cache decisions are easier to reason about and evolve safely
- the highest-value migrations or policy decisions are decomposed into concrete child work

---

## Assignee
`@NotThatKindOfDrLiz`

## Weekly Priority
`P2`

## Weekly Priority Meaning
- `P1` means top priority for the week.
- `P2` means complete this week after P1 priorities are finished.

## Execution Order
1. define target storage/cache direction
2. group and supersede related audit leaves
3. sequence migrations and policy decisions by payoff and risk

## Subgroup
- `@NotThatKindOfDrLiz` — DRI
- `@realmeylisdev` — persistence/caching support
- `@untreu2` — data/repository support

## Coordination
The listed subgroup must review scope, sequencing, and ownership before implementation starts. Coordination may be synchronous or asynchronous. Do not wait for central coordination if the subgroup can resolve the question directly. Escalate only when blocked or when a platform or storage decision is genuinely needed.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this issue as the coordination source of truth for data foundation decisions
- separate immediate execution work from long-horizon design questions
- avoid introducing new storage/caching paths without checking against this direction
- prefer explicit policy over one-off per-feature exceptions

## Engineering Standard
This work must not create new technical debt.

Where relevant, use the audit issues created from PR `#3530` by `@omartinma` as the source of truth for debt repayment and refactor expectations in this area.
